suggestions: Terminology drift: the original's "15-minute lattice" becomes "15-minute grid" (L32, L42, L48). The section defines "grid" as the start times offered, so "keep 15 minutes as the underlying grid" can read as putting every type on a 15-minute grid. That contradicts the working 30-minute default and blurs the distinction the section is built on. The fact still passes on substance.

Added claims not in the original: "smaller, lower-risk engine change" (L42; the original said "smaller and better-behaved"), "two unusable fragments" (L62), "when it's most avoidable" (L56), and "Start or end" a meeting at edges (L40; the original said "anchor").

Added framing: a "Recommendation:" label (L42), "Open issue:" in the 6.5 heading, the 6.3 heading renamed to "Interaction with how slots are ranked", and the open questions turned into a bullet list. These are structural, and consistent with the original.
L93 adds "the model §6.2 recommends against". This cross-reference is accurate.
eval_feedback.overall: 20/20 facts retained. It is the longest output, at 9628 chars against 8053 for new_skill and 6515 for old_skill, so it made the lightest edit. The main risk is lattice->grid terminology drift, plus a few small added intensifiers ("lower-risk", "unusable").
